ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AE is the diameter of the circumscribed circle $\odot O$ of the quadrilateral ABCD, $AD=CD$, $\angle B=50^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle DAE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw OC and OD, \\
$\because$ $\angle B=50^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOC=2\angle B=100^\circ$, \\
$\because$ AD=CD, \\
$\therefore$ $\overset{\frown}{AD}=\overset{\frown}{CD}$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOD=\angle COD= \frac{1}{2}\angle AOC=50^\circ$, \\
$\because$ OA=OD, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle OAD=\angle ODA$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle DAE=(180^\circ-50^\circ)\div2=\boxed{65^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Draw $OC$ and $OD$. Because $\angle B=50^\circ$, $\angle AOC=2\angle B=100^\circ$. Because $AD=CD$, $\overset{\frown}{AD}=\overset{\frown}{CD}$, so $\angle AOD=\angle COD=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOC=50^\circ$. Because $OA=OD$, $\angle OAD=\angle ODA$. Therefore, $\angle DAE=(180^\circ-50^\circ)\div 2=65^\circ$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there is a circle; A, B, C, and D are all on the circle; AE is a horizontal diameter passing through the center O of the circle, with A at the left end and E at the right end; D and C are located near the upper arc, and B is located on the lower-right arc; the chords AB, BC, CD, AD and the diameter AE are also drawn in the figure; the problem gives ∠B=50° and AD=CD.
Reasoning: ∠ABC is an inscribed angle, and what it subtends is the arc AC that does not contain B, namely the arc AC that passes through D, so the corresponding central angle ∠AOC=2∠ABC=100°. Because AD=CD, the arcs subtended by equal chords are equal, so arc AD=arc DC, and the corresponding central angles are also equal, that is, ∠AOD=∠DOC. Also ∠AOC=100°, therefore ∠AOD=∠DOC=50°. In triangle AOD, OA and OD are both radii, so OA=OD, and triangle AOD is an isosceles triangle, hence ∠OAD=∠ODA=(180°−50°)/2=65°. Since O is on AE, ray AO and AE are in the same direction, so ∠DAE=∠DAO=∠OAD=65°.
